thread:
jun: Quick sync — ran onboarding eval for firebrand-emb-v1 (float16 baseline -> int6 quant) on the 10k holdout. High-level: global recall@10 baseline 0.941 -> int6 0.884. Short-query subset (<=6 tokens) recall@1 dropped from 0.81 -> 0.62. Whitening + small rescale recovered to ~0.68. Need triage on the short-query hit.
maya: ouch on short queries. can you paste the eval command/config and the exact metrics? also which quant scheme did you use (per-channel/per-tensor, symmetric/asymmetric)?
jun: sure. command and core output:
```bash
# eval call
python eval/recall.py \
  --model firebrand-emb-v1 \
  --quant int6 \
  --quant-scheme per_channel_symmetric \
  --batch 64 \
  --holdout holdout-10k \
  --shortcut 6
```
Results (top-level):
Recall@1: baseline=0.741, int6=0.612
Recall@5: baseline=0.871, int6=0.833
Recall@10: baseline=0.941, int6=0.884
Short-query (<=6 tokens) Recall@1: baseline=0.81 -> int6=0.62
Silhouette score (anchor clusters): baseline=0.42 -> int6=0.39
ARI (labels vs clusters): baseline=0.27 -> int6=0.24

notes: used per-channel symmetric quant, 2048-sample calibration set drawn from training corpus with length stratification.
anand: thanks. two quick questions: 1) did you quantize the final layernorm/gamma/bias? 2) were embeddings L2-normalized before nearest-neighbor? those can matter a lot for short queries.
jun: we left layernorm in fp16 (no quant), only linear weights int6. embeddings were NOT L2-normalized in the eval pipeline (we were comparing raw vector space). I re-ran a small check adding L2-normalize at query time and Recall@1 for short queries jumped to 0.67 (int6), baseline 0.83.
maya: that suggests geometry shift rather than catastrophic information loss. can you try a tiny calibration trick: compute a whitening matrix on the calibration set + apply per-feature rescale (stddev) before L2-norm? that worked in earlier int8 runs.
jun: tried whitening + rescale; short-query Recall@1 improved to ~0.68, overall recall@10 to 0.892. attaching the short csv snippet ->
```csv
query_len,recall1_base,recall1_int6,recall1_int6_whiten
1-3,0.72,0.49,0.55
4-6,0.86,0.68,0.75
7-15,0.90,0.82,0.84
>15,0.94,0.91,0.92
```
eva: useful breakdown. we should also check idflip rate and k-NN stability (how often top-1 changes rank between baseline and quant). short queries can be dominated by very sparse tokenization signals.
ops-bot: perf note: int6 runtime on staging measured +1.7x token throughput (batch 64) and 28% lower GPU memory. canary rollout would hit ~30% capacity reduction if we switch to int6 across dedicated pools.
anand: action items I suggest:
- run per-channel vs per-tensor int6 sweep (jun) — get recall stratified by query length and language (en/es/pt) and idflip counts
- run variant with L2-normalize only at search time vs both train+search (maya)
- produce UMAP/TSNE anchors for the 2k anchor set to visually inspect cluster drift (maya)
- try quantizing final LN into fp8 vs keep fp16 (anand)
- ops to prepare staging canary with fallback to fp16 model (ops-bot)

jun: assigning: @anand i'll ping you the run ids and the calibration set link. @maya can you do the UMAP + a quick silhouette by query-length split? @ops-bot can we schedule a 2-hour staging canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC with rollback = immediate? ci-bot — please attach the eval logs to the run.

ci-bot: run 2026-02-09T14:22:45Z uploaded logs -> https://internal.ci/firebrand/runs/20260209-142245 (artifacts: recall.csv, embeddings.npy, umap.png)

maya: I'll start UMAP + make a small html scatter with anchors colored by query-length bucket and label density. if clusters collapse for <=3 tokens that's a red flag for representation collapse.
eva: don't forget cross-lingual recall test — short queries in other langs often degrade differently. also run a small semantic-sim test (STS-B like) to track cosine correlations.
jun: noted. timeline: per-channel sweep and idflip audit by EOD tomorrow; UMAP + html by noon; staging canary scheduled. we'll reconvene after those runs and decide whether to accept int6 with whitening patch or require fp16 for short queries. :rocket:
maya: thanks — will post the UMAP link when ready.
anand: I'll try per-tensor int6 as a control; if per-tensor reduces variance on short queries it might be worth the extra perf hit.
ops-bot: created staging canary ticket INF-8342, assigned to eng-ml. rollback policy set to fallback-model=firebrand-emb-v1-fp16.
